studies.Reference: Prospective study of dietary supplements, macronutrients, micronutrients, and risk of bladder cancer in US men.
studies.Title: Prospective study of dietary supplements, macronutrients, micronutrients, and risk of bladder cancer in US men.
studies.Authors: Michaud DS, Spiegelman D, Clinton SK, Rimm EB, Willett WC, Giovannucci E
studies.Timing: 12 years of follow-up; diet assessed in 1986 and 1990
studies.Population: Male health professionals in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study
studies.comparison_type: Dietary potassium intake categories (high vs low), qualitative report of no association

cases.excerpt: During 12 years of follow-up, 320 cases of bladder cancer were diagnosed.

comparison.excerpt: we found no relation for dietary intake of potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, phosphorus, iron, or water-soluble vitamins and bladder cancer risk

design.excerpt: the prospective Health Professionals Follow-Up Study

continent.excerpt: risk of bladder cancer in US men

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Each participant completed a 131-item food frequency questionnaire in 1986 and in 1990, from which nutrient intakes were calculated.

gender.excerpt: the risk of bladder cancer among men
